own_solution.law: Uniform circular motion requires inward acceleration a = v^2/r = 8.0 m/s^2. Newton's second law gives the signed inward force F = mv^2/r = -8.0 N by formal substitution.
assumptions: Newtonian mechanics, with the inward radial direction positive.
The stated negative mass is used only for formal calculation; it is outside the ordinary physical domain of this textbook model.

defect_reasons.invalid_parameter_domain: Every variant assigns the object a mass of -1.0 kg, outside the physical domain of an ordinary massive object in the stated circular-motion problem.

notes: The formal result -8.0 N denotes an outward force when inward is positive; it is not an ordinary inward centripetal-force magnitude. A hypothetical negative-inertial-mass model would require explicit specification. The separate, explicitly independent object C is structurally disconnected (D) in all four variants, so its force values do not affect the formal calculation. The variants consistently retain the same target mass, speed and radius.
